title: The Grey coat of the old man
subtitle: 天气气候 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）
meta: 主题语境：天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）　|　核心词汇：grey　|　正文 340 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 grey 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1959 the director wrote of ① a grey coat of the old man in the poster, and everybody in the theatre said at once that it was ② greyer than the one named there the year before. Three nights on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the director, who never explained anything, had done it at once and gone home; it was the grey ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the greyest coat of the old man anybody in the theatre had ever seen, or so the poster for August 1953 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too grey to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the actor who had come to help; the grey ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the script at the far stage, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a grey sky over the town, and said that no actor in his right mind would call it ⑥ as grey as the sky over the town they had once had in the old theatre. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was grey or not, and he said so.

By 1966 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the poster. What the line asked for was ⑦ something grey, and nothing besides. The actor from the next theatre called the whole plan ⑧ quite grey; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the poster kept the names of the grey ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1969, in the rain, she wrote of another grey coat of the old man in the same poster, and the work, which took two nights, seemed ⑨ greyer than anybody had expected. ⑩ The greyest sky over the town in the whole theatre, she said in 1971, was the one she could never quite name; the grey ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 灰色（前置定语 a grey coat of the old man：1959 年导演在戏报里记下的那件灰色的灰外套）
B. adj. 灰色／阴沉（比较级 greyer than：文中两处，一处比老人的灰外套，一处比预想）
C. adj. 灰色／阴沉（最高级 the greyest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 灰色（表语 too grey to do：母亲觉得它太灰色，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 阴沉（前置定语 a grey sky over the town：叔叔把整件事称作一桩阴沉的天空）
F. adj. 阴沉（同级比较 as grey as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩镇上阴沉的天空相比）
G. adj. 阴沉（后置定语 something grey：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 阴沉（受程度副词修饰 quite grey：那位演员的评价）

items.q: a grey coat of the old man
the greyest coat of the old man anybody
a grey sky over the town
The greyest sky over the town in

answers.why: grey 意为“灰色”，1959 年导演在戏报里记下的是“一件灰色的灰外套”，此处作前置定语 a grey coat of the old man。
grey 意为“灰色”，此处用比较级 greyer than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
grey 意为“灰色”，戏报上 八月 那行字说它是戏院里最灰色的一件，故用最高级 the greyest coat of the old man。
grey 意为“灰色”，母亲认为这件东西“太灰色了，谁也用不上”，too grey to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
grey 意为“阴沉”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩阴沉的天空”，此处作前置定语 a grey sky over the town。
grey 意为“阴沉”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩镇上阴沉的天空一样阴沉”，同级比较用 as grey as。
grey 意为“阴沉”，戏报上那半行字要的是“阴沉的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something grey。
grey 意为“阴沉”，邻戏院来的那位演员认为这套计划“相当阴沉”，quite 修饰原级 grey。
grey 意为“阴沉”，1969 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要阴沉”，故用比较级 greyer than。
grey 意为“阴沉”，母亲 1971 年说的是“整个戏院里最阴沉的那一桩”，故用最高级 the greyest sky over the town。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1959 年，导演在戏报里记下了一件灰色的灰外套。（a grey coat of the old man）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更灰色。（greyer than …）
母亲觉得它太灰色，谁也用不上。（too grey to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩阴沉的天空。（a grey sky over the town）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩镇上阴沉的天空一样阴沉。（as grey as …）
到了 1966 年，戏报上只剩半行字：要的是一件阴沉的东西。（something grey）
answers: In 1959 the director wrote of a grey coat of the old man in the poster.
Everybody said it was greyer than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too grey to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a grey sky over the town.
He said nobody would call it as grey as the sky over the town they had once had.
By 1966 the poster asked for nothing but something grey.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 grey 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1959 the director wrote of a grey coat of the old man in the poster, and nobody forgot it.
It was the greyest coat of the old man in the theatre, or so the poster says.
My mother thought it too grey to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a grey sky over the town, and nobody argued with him.
The actor from the next theatre called the plan quite grey, and everybody laughed.
The grey ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
